title: Raymond Scott and the beard
summary: Scott fires him over a beard.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: And Raymond Scott used to write -- I played with him for a while, too, on the Lucky Strike Program, and he would write an arrangement and he would say, 'come on, make it sound like Basie.' And I would say, 'you don't write like Basie.' He said, 'that doesn't make any difference, play it so it sounds' -- then he'd say, 'well, maybe we won't make this one sound like Basie, we'll make this one sound like Ellington.' And he got these simple little harmonies in there.
I remember him, the guy with that one ... uh ... one ... huh little count, and he'd count up front, one, two, count it off something like that.
He always wore those earphones because

he had a metronome in the clients booth, and he'd have a guy in there who'd set the tempo and he would beat that stick. Remember, he had the downbeat, he'd hold both hands straight out and then when the other hand came level, you started. It was about as inspiring as a cold cod lying there.

Oh, yeah, he was very mathematical. He fired me off the Lucky Strike Show because I grew a beard and that was before beards were popular, that was in the '40s and '50s. They kept following him around, he says, 'you want to know why I fired you?' I said, no, I don't want to know, I did the best I could and you fired me, that's your business and I don't really care why you fired me. He said, 'I'm going to tell you why I fired you, you grew a beard and you wouldn't shave it off.' I said, 'Raymond, I don't care why you fired me. The point is, you fired me. That's the reality. I don't care about the reasons.' I did as good as I can and I couldn't do anything different.
So after I got fired from two more shows, I shaved it off.
